did_you_know.text: Did you know? The phrase “after this” indicates that the promise of pouring out the Spirit will come after the events mentioned earlier in the chapter, describing a future stage of redemption.
Did you know? The prophecy emphasizes that “all flesh” may be affected by the Spirit of the Lord, explicitly mentioning sons and daughters, old men and young men.

Did you know? The Spirit of the Lord is not limited to free people: the verse explicitly mentions male and female servants, thereby extending the circle of those who receive the Spirit to all social classes.
Did you know? The chapter describes three ways in which revelation will come: prophecy, dreams, and visions, associating them with different age groups.
Did you know? Before the day of the Lord, signs are described both in the heavens and on the earth, including blood, fire, and columns of smoke.

Did you know? The description of the sun turning to darkness and the moon to blood presents a dramatic change in the heavenly lights, occurring before the coming of “the great and awesome day of the Lord.”
Did you know? According to the verse, calling on the name of the Lord is connected with deliverance, while Mount Zion and Jerusalem are presented as places where survivors will remain.
Did you know? The verse also mentions “survivors”—those who remain—and concludes that they are the ones whom the Lord calls.
